paragraphs: Posted by Tom. This week, my physics class measured a shadow on the school sports field. Teacher Nick told each pair of students to put a long stick in the ground. My partner was Ben, and we are both aged thirteen. It was a quiet morning, and the grass was green. We were happy to be outside, and we put on our hats. Each pair had a ruler, a notebook, and a raincoat in a bag, because rain might come later. We were especially careful with the notebook, because Teacher Nick checks every number.

First, we measured the shadow of our stick at nine o'clock, and it was forty centimeters long. Ben wrote the number in the notebook, and I held the ruler. We worked slowly and carefully. At ten o'clock, the shadow was thirty centimeters long. At eleven o'clock, it was twenty centimeters long. At twelve o'clock, it was only ten centimeters long. Ben looked at me and smiled.

After lunch, we measured again. We ate rice and chicken under a tree. Then we went back to the stick. It was in the same place. At one o'clock, the shadow was twenty centimeters long. At two o'clock, it was thirty centimeters long, and at three o'clock, it was forty centimeters long. Ben drew a small picture of each number in the notebook. The picture looked like a long, thin letter V. I laughed, and Teacher Nick came to look.

Teacher Nick said, "A shadow is long when the sun is low." He also said, "A shadow is short when the sun is high." "Look at your numbers," he said, "and think about the sun." Other pairs had almost the same numbers as we did. One pair had a bad stick, and its shadow was too short, so its numbers were wrong. Ben and I wrote a short report at the end of the day. Ben wrote his name on the first page. I wrote mine on the last page.

"Can we do this experiment on a cloudy day?" asked Ben. "No," said Teacher Nick. "It is impossible to measure a shadow without sun." We were lucky, because we saw the sun all day, and nobody used a raincoat. I like physics because we work outside, and I like Ben as my partner.
